options.content:
### DB Query Traces — jump from a latency spike to the exact slow SQL trace

SQL spans already exist: **otelpgx** in `refdata-api` / `oeecloud-worker` / `operator-adapter`, and `edge-api` auto-instruments `pg`. Every DB span carries `span.db.system = "postgresql"` and `span.db.statement` (the SQL text). This board is pure **TraceQL** against the Tempo datasource (`packiot-tempo`).

**Workflow:** latency panel (board 12 API / board 11 DB) shows a spike → click the exemplar dot → land on the trace here → open the span → read `db.statement`. Or start here: filter recent slow DB spans, click a Trace ID, then use the span's *Logs* / *Metrics* links (Tempo → Loki / Prometheus correlation) to see the surrounding context.

🟡 **Truthful-empty caveat:** exemplar *dots* on Prometheus latency panels stay absent until each service ATTACHES its active `trace_id` as an exemplar on `http_request_duration_seconds` (per-service code = separate PR). The trace **search** panels below work today regardless — Tempo already receives the spans. `mirror-worker-go` and `shadow-mirror` are **untraced (retiring)** workers — expect no spans from them by design.

panels.title: Recent slow DB spans  ( db.system=postgresql && duration > $min_dur )
panels.description: TraceQL: { span.db.system = "postgresql" && duration > $min_dur }. Click a Trace ID to open the trace; the span's db.statement holds the SQL. Sorted by duration.

panels.title: SQL latency p95 by service (TraceQL metrics)
panels.description: TraceQL metrics: { span.db.system="postgresql" } | quantile_over_time(duration, .95) by (resource.service.name). Requires Tempo metrics-generator / local-blocks. One line per service that emits pg spans.

panels.title: SQL span rate by service (TraceQL metrics)
panels.description: TraceQL metrics: { span.db.system="postgresql" } | rate() by (resource.service.name). DB span throughput per service — pairs with the p95 panel to separate 'slow' from 'busy'.

panels.title: Saved: refdata-api slow pg spans ( > 200ms )
panels.description: Exemplar TraceQL: { resource.service.name = "refdata-api" && span.db.system="postgresql" && duration > 200ms }. refdata-api is the hot read plane — this is the first place to look when the front4→refdata read path is slow.

panels.title: Saved: spans touching equipment_runtime_shift
panels.description: Exemplar TraceQL: { span.db.statement =~ ".*equipment_runtime_shift.*" }. Find-slow-queries-BY-TABLE via a db.statement regex — the OEE shift-rollup table is a frequent hotspot. Until a first-class db.sql.table attribute is emitted (separate per-service PR), regex on the statement text is the way to filter by table.

panels.title: TraceQL cookbook — find slow queries by table

options.content:
## TraceQL cookbook

All queries run against the **Tempo** datasource (`packiot-tempo`). Paste into an Explore → Tempo → *TraceQL* tab, or edit a panel above. Duration literals: `ms`, `s` (e.g. `100ms`, `1.5s`).

### Core building blocks
| Intent | TraceQL |
|---|---|
| Any Postgres span | `{ span.db.system = "postgresql" }` |
| Slow DB spans | `{ span.db.system = "postgresql" && duration > 100ms }` |
| Slow DB spans in one service | `{ resource.service.name = "refdata-api" && span.db.system = "postgresql" && duration > 200ms }` |
| Traces that contain a slow DB span (span→trace) | `{ span.db.system = "postgresql" && duration > 500ms } | select(resource.service.name)` |

### Find slow queries BY TABLE (regex on db.statement)
There is **no `db.sql.table` attribute yet** (adding one is a per-service code PR — see the compose `# TODO`). Until then, match the table name inside the SQL text with a regex:

| Table | TraceQL |
|---|---|
| `equipment_runtime_shift` | `{ span.db.statement =~ ".*equipment_runtime_shift.*" }` |
| …and slow only | `{ span.db.statement =~ ".*equipment_runtime_shift.*" && duration > 100ms }` |
| `production_orders` writes | `{ span.db.statement =~ "(?i).*(insert into\|update).*production_orders.*" }` |
| any `equipment_values` scan | `{ span.db.statement =~ ".*equipment_values.*" }` |

**Caveats of the regex approach:** (1) case-sensitive by default — prefix `(?i)` for case-insensitive; (2) matches the statement text, so a table named in a comment or a JOIN also matches; (3) escape regex metacharacters in table names. A future `db.sql.table` attribute (via `otelpgx.WithIncludeQueryParameters` + a table-extracting span processor) would make this `{ span.db.sql.table = "equipment_runtime_shift" }` — exact, indexed, cheap.

### TraceQL metrics (rate / quantile over time)
| Intent | TraceQL |
|---|---|
| p95 DB latency by service | `{ span.db.system="postgresql" } | quantile_over_time(duration, .95) by (resource.service.name)` |
| DB span rate by service | `{ span.db.system="postgresql" } | rate() by (resource.service.name)` |
| Slow-span rate for one table | `{ span.db.statement =~ ".*equipment_runtime_shift.*" && duration > 100ms } | rate()` |

### From a trace, jump sideways (already wired on the Tempo datasource)
- **→ Logs (Loki):** span *Logs* link filters `packiot-loki` by trace id (`tracesToLogsV2`).
- **→ Metrics (Prometheus):** span *Metrics* link (`tracesToMetrics`) + the service map (`serviceMap`).
- **← from Prometheus:** once services attach `trace_id` exemplars, latency panels on boards 11/12 show clickable dots that land here (`exemplarTraceIdDestinations`).

### Instrumented vs. not
| Service | pg spans? |
|---|---|
| `refdata-api`, `oeecloud-worker`, `operator-adapter` | ✅ otelpgx |
| `edge-api` | ✅ pg auto-instrumentation |
| `mirror-worker-go`, `shadow-mirror` | 🟡 untraced — **retiring**, will not be instrumented |
